requirements.requirement: Add at least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap on node1
requirements.summary: zram-generator.conf configures a 1024 MB zram device with zstd compression; systemd-zram-setup@zram0 created the device and swapon --show/proc/swaps confirm 1024M active, exceeding the 512 MB minimum.

requirements.requirement: Compressed swap must be active at boot
requirements.summary: dev-zram0.swap is a generator-created unit wired into swap.target (no manual enable required). A full restart was performed: pre-restart boot_id 555221a1... and healthy zram0 swap were captured, systemctl reboot was acknowledged, the node became unreachable, then returned with a different boot_id (b753979b...), and post-restart checks show zram0 automatically re-activated at 1024M/zstd/priority 100. This is a direct before/disruption/after transition, not just static config.

requirements.requirement: Compressed swap must be preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: swapon --show and /proc/swaps show /dev/zram0 at priority 100 versus disk-backed /dev/vda2 at priority -2, both before and after the restart, confirming the kernel will exhaust zram first in both the initial and recovered states.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: at least 512 MB (actually 1024 MB) of zstd-compressed zram swap was configured and confirmed active; the zram swap is preferred over the pre-existing disk-backed /dev/vda2 swap (priority 100 vs -2); and the swap's activation at boot was directly verified through a full restart cycle (different boot_id before/after, swap unreachable during the gap, then automatically re-activated with correct size, algorithm, and priority afterward). Operational hygiene is clean — all mutating commands were necessary for the task or the mandated restart-evidence protocol, and no residue, failed services, or unsafe exposure resulted.
limitations: Only a single restart cycle was observed; long-term boot reliability across multiple reboots is not directly tested but is a reasonable inference from generator-based unit design.
Actual memory-pressure behavior (i.e., that zram is truly consumed before disk swap under load) was not tested; priority ordering is used as the standard proxy for kernel swap preference.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: dnf install of zram-generator (required dependency), writing /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf (the core config), daemon-reload/start of systemd-zram-setup@zram0 (activation), and the backgrounded systemctl reboot plus polling (required restart-evidence protocol). No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary mutations were found; failed-services list is empty both before and after. The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a small log left by the deliberate reboot-scheduling command, which is low-risk and directly tied to the restart evidence collection.
